{{ElectionsCA}}

On November 20, 2023, the [[San Francisco Board of Supervisors]] passed a motion ordering the inclusion of '''Proposition G: Offering Algebra 1 to Eighth Graders''' on the '''March 2024 Local Ballot'''.<ref name="SF Gov">{{Cite web |title=Proposition G: Offering Algebra 1 to Eighth Graders |publisher=San Francisco government |url=https://www.sf.gov/information/proposition-g-offering-algebra-1-eighth-graders |access-date=2024-02-14}}</ref> Written by Supervisor [[Joel Engardio]], the measure acts as a [[Non-binding resolution|non-binding policy statement]] urging the [[San Francisco Unified School District]] to reverse their decision on delaying enrollment in [[Algebra|Algebra I]] until ninth grade.<ref name="Official Motion" /> The measure passed with 81.75% of the vote.<ref name="Ballotpedia">{{Cite web |title=San Francisco, California, Proposition G, Declaration of Policy Urging San Francisco Unified School District to Offer Algebra 1 to Students by Eighth Grade Measure (March 2024) |url=https://ballotpedia.org/San_Francisco,_California,_Proposition_G,_Declaration_of_Policy_Urging_San_Francisco_Unified_School_District_to_Offer_Algebra_1_to_Students_by_Eighth_Grade_Measure_(March_2024) |access-date=2024-05-25 |website=[[Ballotpedia]]}}</ref> The passage of the measure did not immediately change course offerings for students. The San Francisco Unified School District is a [[Government agency|public agency]] that is separate from the City and retains [[jurisdiction]] in regards to when Algebra I is able to be offered to students.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Schwartz |first=Sarah |date=2023-03-20 |title=San Francisco Insisted on Algebra in 9th Grade. Did It Improve Equity? |url=https://www.edweek.org/teaching-learning/san-francisco-insisted-on-algebra-in-9th-grade-did-it-improve-equity/2023/03 |access-date=2024-02-14 |work=Education Week |language=en |issn=0277-4232}}</ref> Passage of the proposal would inform the San Francisco Unified School District on the stance of the constituents in regards to their preferred math offerings for students.<ref name="Official Motion">{{Cite web |last=City and County of San Francisco Department of Elections |title=Official Motion |url=https://www.sf.gov/sites/default/files/2023-11/DecofPolicyEighthGradeAlgebraandSFUSDMathCurriculumDevelopment.pdf?_gl=1*1x4ijj7*_ga*MTkzMzAxMzUzMy4xNzA2OTA3MjM0*_ga_BT9NDE0NFC*MTcwNzkyODYyMy44LjEuMTcwNzkyODY1MS4wLjAuMA..*_ga_63SCS846YP*MTcwNzkyODYyMy44LjEuMTcwNzkyODY1MS4wLjAuMA..}}</ref> Additionally, the proposal would: support the School District's development of its [[Curriculum|math curriculum]] for students at all grade levels, explore [[Differentiated instruction|differentiation]] options for students both below and above grade-level in math across all grades, and promote pathways for students interested in studying [[Science, technology, engineering, and mathematics|STEM]] at the [[university]] level.<ref name="SF Gov" />

== Results ==
The election was held on March 5, 2024. Proposition G passed with 81.75% of the vote, receiving 182,066 "Yes" votes and 40,638 "No" votes.<ref name="Ballotpedia" />
